title: Quasi-compact subsets of a Hausdorff space are closed, and disjoint quasi-compact subsets can be separated by open sets

standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of quasi-compactness for subsets with the induced topology, and the Hausdorff separation axiom

standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the hypothesis on the space and the two conclusions about quasi-compact subsets.

core_obligations: Part (1): given a point x outside a quasi-compact subset E, the proof separates x from each point of E by disjoint open sets, extracts a finite subcover of E from the resulting covering, and intersects the finitely many open neighbourhoods of x to obtain an open neighbourhood of x disjoint from E, so E is closed (proof lines 1904-1910).

Part (2): for two disjoint quasi-compact subsets the proof applies part (1) to each point of the first subset, obtaining an open neighbourhood of it disjoint from the second, extracts finitely many such neighbourhoods that cover the first subset, and then intersects the corresponding finitely many neighbourhoods of the second subset (proof lines 1910-1919).
Conclusion: the two numbered assertions of the statement (proof line 1919).
proof_roadmap: (1) 对 E 外一点 x，用 Hausdorff 性对 E 的每点取与 x 分离的不交开集，取出有限子覆盖，再过 x 的有限多个邻域取交，得与 E 不交的开邻域，故 E 闭。
(2) 对 E_1 的每点用 (1) 得到与 E_2 不交的开邻域，取有限子覆盖后，对 E_2 的相应有限多个邻域取交即得。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the standard compactness-separation lemma in a Hausdorff space (author lemma at source lines 1893-1901, label lemma-quasi-compact-in-Hausdorff): quasi-compact subsets are closed, and two disjoint quasi-compact subsets have disjoint open neighbourhoods. The proof (source lines 1903-1920) is the classical double compactness argument, written out in full: the first part separates a point from a quasi-compact set by finitely many neighbourhoods (proof lines 1904-1910), and the second part iterates the first over the points of one of the two subsets and then takes a finite intersection on the other side (proof lines 1910-1919). The lemma is used throughout the chapter when separatedness of quasi-compact pieces is needed. H2.
